decision: Retain prototype for parent review: whole encounter window including real first construction and post-handoff frames improves substantially. No claim of sustained native residence after revision or equal-load native algorithm speedup.
scope: No production layout or native DLL changes. Only shared-step galaxy preflight, removal of blanket active-galaxy admission rejection, and live collision-host binding at handoff.
A is the existing cold-admission rejection path; B admits native then hands off before the first real revision. These are different execution paths, not two native implementations.

All windows include >=12 game seconds, real opening revision, and post-opening behavior. No fast-only cut. Same ordinary galaxy configuration and one assigned crew; no artificial accelerated construction or resource history.
A1/A2 failed real-time throughput: about0.244 game/wall. B ratio0.9715 is near real1x but not exact60Hz; all retain nominal60Hz and speed1. No reduced frequency or projectile cap.

B fires/hits and instantaneous projectile counts differ; do not call it equal hit workload. Existing fixed presentation is activated by native admission and retained after handoff, while cold legacy follows its existing path.
B native residence is lower-bound sampled at frame ends. Handoff frame is grouped with legacy and may contain native work.
Post-handoff B is still slow (~144ms/frame over17 frames); this prototype does not solve long-encounter legacy cost or guarantee >1ms savings for arbitrary initial building phases.
Earlier interrupted comparison had unbound legacy collision-host errors and is excluded. Final completed round has no SCRIPT ERROR.
Mixed final-work/construction/upgrading test confirmed progress includes construction; no production change required for the reviewed hypothesis.
Screenshot is the end of B after handoff; its FPS label reflects late legacy frames, not the entire-window average.
